question.worked_solution:
To find the rank of $A,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ -6 & -9 & -4 \\ 4 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 4 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $2$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(A)=2.$
